title: Parades with uniforms and grand marshal; a note on Punch Miller
summary: He never worked with Punch on the road; shows paraded in red coats behind a grand marshal with police escort.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, Punch used to play some of those carnival shows too and told us something about him. Did you ever play with Punch on a, run across him on the road?
No, I never played with Punch on the road. No, never have. But I have played a few jobs that is occasionally around in town.
Yeah. Yeah. I was going to ask a bit more about the parades. What did they do? Go right through the main part of town. Did they have any uniforms or manners?

Oh yeah. We had long red coats that we wore. And had the name of the show, wrote in the back of the coach. And we always had a man that is, we always had a grand marshal with the show. Yeah. Grand marshal that was, well, he would dress, put on his funny looking uniform and he would do a lot of performing in front of the band. Yeah. Well, he would lead us right on through town. As soon as we hit town, in fact, two weeks before we hit the town, the man of the show, he'd be done, got permission, you know, to parade at such and such a time. And most of the time, motorcycle cops would be waiting for us. We would just follow them right on through town. Anything in the back of the band?
I mean, any other performers or any trucker or wagon?
Flunk or whatever you want to call it. We had a flunk.
